quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: In crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by the car driver failing to give the motorcycle rider the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver does not give the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of these should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and avoid moving around so you can focus on riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When being passed, you should not move to the far side of your lane because it:

options.text: Discourages the passing driver from cutting back into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to cut back into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to finish the pass quickly.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourages the passing driver to cut back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane can encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen the most?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.explanation: Bright colors help other drivers see you. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green works best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than walking speed, your motorcycle leans into turns. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn to lean the motorcycle correctly.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Not be used.
Be on high beam.
Be on low beam.
Switch between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Using your high beam during the day helps other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When braking in a curve:

options.text: Only use the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it requires extra care. When leaning to turn, some of your tire's grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Exit the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a wet lane is especially dangerous. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars to avoid the slippery center. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or use saddlebags. Placing loads high on the back raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and throws off balance. Spread loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which of these can be a rectangular sign?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These are regulatory signs. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group
Just behind the lead rider
At the back of the group
Anywhere in the group

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other
Do both actions at the same time
Always brake first, then swerve
Use only the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve separately, not at the same time. You can brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder
Use the left portion of your lane
Use the center portion of your lane
Use the right portion of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is safest when being passed. Staying too close to the passing vehicle risks collision. Staying too far away might make the driver pull back too soon.

questions.question: How do you get maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the rear brake only
Use the front brake only
Use both brakes
Use the rear brake while downshifting

questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: As weight shifts to the front of your motorcycle while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Gradually increase front brake pressure
Use more rear brake pressure
Don't worry. Weight transfer won't affect your motorcycle
Try to lock the front tire

questions.explanation: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward during braking, slowly increase pressure on the front brake lever.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader
In front of the group
At the back of the group
Beside the leader

questions.explanation: Place inexperienced riders toward the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing inexperienced riders to lead.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane
Move to the left portion of the lane
Move to the right portion of the lane
Don't worry about which lane portion you use

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases collision risk.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
You can see hazards in the next lane more clearly.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
The car in front will see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see hazards in the next lane more clearly.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane gives you a better view of the road ahead. This position also makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Riders who wear helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries in a crash, at any speed.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Riding jackets protect you and help prevent dehydration. Many jackets are made to keep you cool in warm weather while still providing protection.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Increase your following distance.
Communicate with the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle will respond more slowly. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it signals a right turn or lane change to the right. Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals.
